result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by industrial land use, featuring a wide gated driveway that interrupts the sidewalk. While the sidewalk itself is in good condition, there is a complete lack of markings or signage to manage conflicts between pedestrians and heavy vehicles entering or exiting the site.

hazards.name: Wide Industrial Driveway
hazards.description: A wide gated entrance for trucks crosses the sidewalk, creating a conflict zone without clear pedestrian priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Fencing and storage containers adjacent to the sidewalk may block sightlines between pedestrians and vehicles exiting the lot.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the fence line

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Paint a high-visibility crosswalk across the driveway to clearly define the pedestrian path and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Watch for Pedestrians' signs at the exit of the industrial lot to improve driver awareness.

result.summary: The street environment is highly hostile to pedestrians, lacking dedicated sidewalks and marked crossings. Pedestrians are forced to share the roadway with vehicles, and parked cars further restrict the available walking space and sightlines.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved sidewalks on either side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk in the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the visible area

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles, particularly the large white van on the right, block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground and left mid-ground

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The roadway surface is cracked and uneven, creating potential tripping hazards for pedestrians sharing the road.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center roadway

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicular traffic.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Parking Restrictions
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near potential crossing points to improve visibility and clear the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and repave the roadway to provide a smooth, safe surface for all users.

result.summary: The residential street features sidewalks on both sides but lacks basic crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps. Pedestrian safety is compromised by a large vehicle parked near the corner that severely obstructs sightlines and utility poles that narrow the walkway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A large white truck is parked immediately at the corner, blocking the view of oncoming traffic for pedestrians and the view of pedestrians for drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground at the intersection corner

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is situated in the middle of the sidewalk path, creating a barrier for those with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate a pedestrian crossing area at this intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the roadway

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to improve sightlines between motorists and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra or ladder style crosswalk markings to clearly delineate pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install sloped curb ramps with tactile paving to provide an accessible path of travel.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a residential street lacking basic safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps. While sidewalks are present, they are in fair to poor condition with visible cracking and obstructions like utility poles.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected space to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk ends at a vertical curb without ramps, creating a significant barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk on the left

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the corner may block the visibility between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.
